About me

I build backends.
Mostly in Python.

Backend Engineer · Python, Data & ML Systems
Kolkata, India · Open to remote

I build backend systems for data that does not fit in memory, and for models that should not be trusted blindly.

I did not set out to work on brains. I set out to work as a backend engineer, and the role that found me happened to involve EEG. Clinical recordings can be large enough for one careless query to exhaust memory. Processing them in windows can change the result without throwing an error. Someone may use that output to make a decision about a patient.

Models propose. Deterministic code decides.

In Tempo, a local model drafts tasks but a typed Python service owns the dates and schedule. In Premiere Assist, FFmpeg supplies evidence to a resolver that writes the edit list; the model never runs a command. My retrieval system exposes how semantic and exact-term search contribute to each result. I trade flexibility for behaviour I can reproduce and explain.

I would rather write down a decision than assume everyone has the same context. The expensive failures I have watched were rarely technical; they were two people each confident they had already agreed.

My final-year insurance project became a leakage audit when the offline score looked too good. The EEG benchmark came from checking whether processing a short window gave the same answer as processing the whole recording. Those questions are why I keep the measurement conditions beside the numbers.

The habit I am working against is overengineering: building for a scale and a set of cases a system may never meet. Naming it has not cured it, but it has made me slower to reach for the abstraction.

Tools I work with

Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB, Redis, Docker and Azure.
